title: Why does this walk cycle look so cursed?
author: Acceptable_Fix_731
selftext:
I’m pretty new to animation, so I might be missing something obvious here.  
I’ve been making this little ink-wash martial arts prototype and using generative AI to explore the environments and overall style. The chapter switching works now, and I’m mostly happy with how the scenes look.

The character movement is driving me crazy, though.  
I’ve stared at it for too long and can’t tell what’s actually wrong anymore. The feet look like they’re sliding, but the whole body also feels weirdly weightless. It looks more like the character is floating over the painting than walking through it.  
Is this mainly a walk-speed problem, a bad animation, or something I could fix with foot IK? What would you change first?

comments.author: Fun_Score5537
comments.body: Looks like his right legs model is attached to the left legs skeleton, vice versa

comments.author: FailedGradAdmissions
comments.body: Both, speed doesn’t match animation, and the foot animation has bad rigging

comments.author: Nicstar543
comments.body: Your character seems like it’s not center? Every time you change direction there’s a visible displacement from where your character was before, like imagine the center is a circle, your character should be in the middle of the circle but yours looks like it’s on the outer edge of the circle so rotation of the sprite looks off

replies.author: Final_Homework_9491
replies.body: Agreed with this comment, this would be first thing I’d correct

comments.author: Bratchan
comments.body: Speed doesn't match talking. Character model is moving as well as you moving it. So it's moving from its center point as well.

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectful. Removed for AI Art or Artist bashing.

comments.author: erofamiliar
comments.body:
It probably needs to be completely redone. The walk speed is wrong, but the animation is also broken, and "fixing it with IK" would basically mean completely redoing it with IK.

My advice: If it doesn't look good in Blender, it won't look good in engine. If you can't get it to work in Blender, you won't get it to work well in engine either, or be able to fix any remaining issues with it.
